findings.message: This only fixes the named instance of the UTC 'today' finding. The previous round named two copies: `isoDate(new Date())` in log.ts and `today()` in ui/parts.tsx. The diff removes the server default but leaves `today()` alone. MyPage is a server component, so a `today()` default for the log form's day runs on the server and still gives the UTC date. logTime then takes that date as the person's own calendar day, which the README promises it never is. Fix: remove the UTC `today()` default, or work it out in the tenant's or user's time zone. Then add a variant test over UTC+5:30, UTC−8 and UTC.
findings.scenario: Tenant in Asia/Colombo, Monday 2026-10-19 at 04:00 local (Sunday 22:30 UTC). The My timesheet form fills day=2026-10-18 from `today()`. logTime refuses it as a weekend, or, on other days, saves the hours a day early and in the previous ISO week.

findings.message: The two contract reads apply the data scope differently. weekTotals calls `seesWeek` with all of the week's project ids, so a project manager who can see a week gets every hour in it, including hours on other projects. projectHours calls `seesWeek` with only `[projectId]` for each row, so the same viewer sees only their own project. The README says both functions return 'weeks they could see on Team time'. As written they give different totals for the same viewer and the same week. Fix: write one scope rule, either week-level or entry-level, and use it in both. Add a test where a PM's report has hours on a project the PM doesn't manage.
findings.scenario: Ayesha manages FLT. Dinesh logs 30 h on FLT and 10 h on CON in 2026-W42. weekTotals(ayesha) shows Dinesh with 40 h. projectHours(ayesha) for the same range adds up to 30 h (FLT only). The two contracts disagree for one viewer.

findings.message: The test for 'an Admin can't change their own approved week' plants the approved state by hand: `update time.week set status = 'approved', locked_at = now()`. It doesn't go through submitWeek and then approveWeek by another approver. That skips the real lock path, including any approval rows or fields the lock check may depend on. It is also the only case: there is no table of variants (for example, an Admin adding time to their own approved week through MCP as agent time, or through an explicit `userId` equal to their own). Fix: have maya submit and sahan approve through the services, then run the self-change variants in a table.
findings.scenario: If approveWeek sets something guardLock depends on beyond `status`, such as a field written by the approval, this test stays green while the real approved-week path behaves differently.

findings.message: The rule 'an optional week key: absent means latest, malformed is an error' now exists three times: `wantedWeek` in server/weeks.ts and a local `weekParam` in both TeamPage.tsx and MyPage.tsx. The two `weekParam` copies use `parseWeekKey(...) ?? notFound()` directly instead of going through weekOrNow. They agree today, but they will drift if weekOrNow's validation changes. Fix: have both pages call one shared helper, for example wantedWeek wrapped to turn its error into notFound().

The 'more than one <name>' error lists the email of every namesake with a timesheet that week. findWeek throws it before checking whether the caller may see or decide those weeks. Any caller of approve_week, reject_week, remind_week or reopen_week can get other people's emails by naming them. Fix: list only the rows the caller can see, or leave the emails out.
findings.scenario: A manager whose only report is Kasun calls remind_week with person='Nimal Silva' while two Nimal Silvas outside their scope have timesheets. The error shows both people's emails.

findings.message: The README now says reminders go out as events only, with no notification rule, and leaves the rule to 030. Meanwhile the Remind button and the remind_week tool tell the user a reminder was sent, so the person is never actually reminded. architecture.md says manifest slots that are plain data, including notification rules, need no dependency on the change that consumes them. So time can declare its rule for `time.week.reminded` in module.ts now instead of waiting for 030. Fix: add the rule to the manifest. If that can't be done, stop the Remind action from looking like it succeeded.
findings.scenario: A PM clicks Remind on Tharushi's draft week. `time.week.reminded` is recorded and the button shows success, but no in-app, email or Teams message is ever sent to Tharushi.
